ra: The concept of the Manifestation of God defines the membership category that the collective hub gathers.
The Báb is regarded in Bahá'í doctrine as an independent Manifestation of God.
Bahá'u'lláh is the central Manifestation of God of the present dispensation.
The Báb is an instance of the Mazhar (Manifestation of God) category in Bahá'í prophetology.
Bahá'u'lláh is the supreme exemplar of the Mazhar category for this age.
The Báb is the author/revealer of the Bayán.
The Bayán is the scriptural corpus revealed through the Báb (inverse of the reveals edge; replaces an incorrect reception_of).
Quddús was the eighteenth and foremost of the Letters of the Living.
Táhirih was the only woman among the Letters of the Living.
Quddús was a leading disciple of the Báb.
Táhirih was an early recognizer and disciple of the Báb.
Abdu'l-Bahá was the eldest son of Bahá'u'lláh.
Bahá'u'lláh was the father of Abdu'l-Bahá.
Abdu'l-Bahá was appointed Centre of the Covenant by Bahá'u'lláh.
Shoghi Effendi was appointed Guardian and authorized interpreter within the line of the Covenant.
Shoghi Effendi was appointed Guardian by Abdu'l-Bahá's Will and Testament.
The Bahá'í Covenant derives its authority from Bahá'u'lláh's appointment of successors (replaces an incorrect reception_of).
The Universal House of Justice was ordained by Bahá'u'lláh in the Kitáb-i-Aqdas (replaces an incorrect reception_of).
The Universal House of Justice is the institution charged with the Covenant after the Guardianship.
The Hands of the Cause functioned prominently under Shoghi Effendi's guidance.
Bahá'u'lláh is identified by Bahá'ís as the fulfillment of the Báb's prophecy of 'Him Whom God shall make manifest.'
Bahá'í progressive revelation regards Bahá'u'lláh's dispensation as renewing the religion of prior Manifestations including Abraham.
Bahá'í doctrine treats Moses as a prior Manifestation whose revelation is fulfilled in Bahá'u'lláh's.
Bahá'ís regard Jesus as a Manifestation of God whose return is realized spiritually in Bahá'u'lláh's revelation.
Bahá'í teaching honors Muhammad as a Manifestation of God preceding Bahá'u'lláh in the prophetic chain.
Bahá'í progressive revelation counts Zoroaster among the prior Manifestations of God.
Bahá'ís hold the Báb fulfilled Shi'i expectation of the return of the Hidden Imam (Mahdi); functional/eschatological alignment, not identity.
The collective of Manifestations is constituted by the Mazhar prophetological concept.
